issues.description: The problem statement requires that a person's parents be stored as a List ("which must be stored as a `List`"). However, both the template and the solution implement parents and children as Set<Person> (using HashSet). This mismatch can confuse students: they may change the template to use List based on the instructions and then break or diverge from the provided repository/tests (which expect Set semantics and use Set-based assertions in the solution).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. The least intrusive fix is to update the problem statement to require that parents/children are stored as a Set (not a List), since the template, tests, and solution already use Set<Person>. Alternatively, if Lists are intentionally desired, change Person.java in the template and solution (and update tests) to use List<Person> everywhere and adapt persistence mappings accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires that a person's parents "must be stored as a `List`" (Part 4, adding a feature). However, both the template and the solution repositories implement the parents (and children) relationship as a Set<Person> (ManyToMany fields: parents and children). This is a semantic mismatch between the instructional text and the provided code: students reading the problem will expect to work with a List but the codebase (and tests/solution) uses Set. This can cause confusion when students try to map the requirement to the template, and may lead to incorrect local changes or misunderstandings about how to implement/add parents and children.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the problem text and the code. Preferably update the problem statement to state that parents (and children) are stored as a Set<Person> (or otherwise explain the use of a Set in the template and solution and why it differs from a List). Alternatively, change the model and solution to use List<Person> for parents/children and update repository mappings and tests accordingly. The simplest non-invasive fix: modify the problem statement wording from "must be stored as a `List`" to "should be stored in a collection (the template uses a Set<Person>)" and adjust any instructions/tests that assume a List.
